description.narrative:
Fund the creation of Four films and two visual art pieces exploring the intersections of queerness and human rights.
2024: Two Filmakers
2025: One Filmaker/One Visual Artist
2026: One Filmaker/One Visual Artist

The fund received a total of 84 submissions, each showcasing a diverse range of proposals that covered various aspects including project overviews, inspiration, narrative approaches, diversity and inclusivity models, intersectionality, ethical considerations, personal statements, as well as detailed budgets and timelines.
Over the course of a month, the independent panel of jurors reviewed each submission, considering both the artistic merit and the potential impact of the projects, and based on several key criteria: project overview, inspiration, narrative approach, diversity and inclusivity models, intersectionality, ethical considerations, personal statements, budget, and timeline. After thorough deliberation, two outstanding awardees were selected based on their compelling narratives, innovative approaches, and alignment with the fund’s mission. These awardees have been onboarded and have commenced the development of their respective projects. Feedback from the jury underscored the high quality of submissions and the challenging task of selecting only two recipients from such a competitive pool.
Title: UNBURIED Film maker: Ayo Lawson Project Overview: ‘Unburied’ highlights the harrowing journey of a trans protagonist from a conservative Yoruba family and extreme Pentecostal background, set against the backdrop of contemporary Nigeria. As they navigate the difficult path of self-discovery, they confront not only their family’s rejection but also societal transphobia and religious judgments. The story unfolds in a haunting forest, where the protagonist is metaphorically and literally running from their past, embodied by a sinister masquerade that represents their fear, trauma, and the societal urge to erase their identity.
Narrative Approach: This psycho-thriller hybrid uses the elements of suspense and the supernatural to explore the profound human rights issue of LGBTQ+ acceptance in a society that often marginalizes and seeks to bury such voices. ‘Unburied’ is a poignant narrative of struggle, resilience, and the fight for one's right to live authentically. Through its unique storytelling, the film aims to shed light on the challenges faced by transgender and non-binary individuals in Nigeria, highlighting the intersectionality of identity, and advocating for a world that respects and upholds the dignity of all its inhabitants, regardless of gender identity.
Title: TRACES OF THE SUN Film maker: Rete Poki Project Overview: ‘TRACES OF THE SUN is an essay film that aims to confront the nature of the patriarchy, generational trauma, historical revisionism through the framework of love and Nigerian Womanhood. The question- What is love to you, a Nigerian Woman- is the point of departure from which willing participants recount their experiences and perspectives on love as a concept, an ideal, a constant practice or an act of defiance.
Narrative Approach: The backbone of this film are conversations between participants and the audience. To reflect the themes of intimacy and vulnerability, there’ll be recordings of interviews in unconventional but familiar environments that reinforce feelings of ease, security and relaxation; gardens, bedrooms, dining tables, cars and other open spaces. The film will also incorporate archival still imagery, with the consent of participants, to provide a richer representation of their experiences and perspectives.
